title: Trajectory quarterback: 1:1 prep and evidence canvas
content:
Quick framing: use this doc as my running scratchpad for the next two 1:1s with my manager. Goal is to make the conversation evidence-led, concise, and forward-looking. I want to leave with a clear set of experiments (30/60/90d) and one specific ask.

Sections I care about (top of page checklist):
- 3 wins since last sync (metrics + qualitative)
  - reduced time-to-onboard for new hires by ~18% (updated checklist + manager training session) — metric from HR onboarding tracker; anecdote: hiring manager A said first week ramp time felt noticeably better.
  - piloted new calibration rubric in Eng hiring loop; 6 interviews used rubric, hiring decision agreement rose from 62% -> 78% (small n).
  - launched micro-coaching program MVP: 12 volunteers, 9 completed, 7 reported improved first-week confidence in survey.
- 2 signals of risk or drag
  - backlog of post-offer admin tasks still causing 1–2 day delays for comp offers (ops ticket queue length + one escalated case).
  - stretch leadership opportunity is stalled — hiring freeze + unclear prioritization.
- 1 clear ask
  - short ask: 0.5FTE fractional support for offer admin onboarding operations for 3 months (to reduce delays and free headspace for rollout).

Evidence snippets to cite (copy into the meeting):
- onboarding-metrics.csv snapshot (Nov vs Jan): new hire completion 84% -> 97% on checklist; avg first-week tasks completed 3.1 -> 4.6.
- email thread (hiring-manager-A) where they flagged friction and thanked the coach session.
- calibration notes summary: short anonymized table of 6 interviews + pre/post agreement numbers.

Behavioral examples (short stories, punchy):
- Ownership: stopped second-order churn by pairing with infra team to change default offer template; saved ~45 minutes per offer.
- Bias to action: ran two rapid workshops with hiring managers in <10 days to iterate rubric — delivered usable changes within sprint.
- Cross-team influence: persuaded Eng leads to trial micro-coaching by showing quick survey results and a one-page ROI sketch.

Hypotheses for my next 6 months (for calibration & career thread):
- Hypothesis 1: Owning the offer admin flow improvement will unlock 1 FTE-equivalent capacity across recruiting and ops (measurement: backlog length + time-to-accept).
- Hypothesis 2: Demonstrating measurable calibration lift in hiring decisions will create demand for a dedicated hiring-rubric role or partial analyst support.

Proposed experiments (30/60/90) — concrete and measurable:
- 30 day: spin up a temporary offer-admin playbook + 0.2 FTE contractor for triage; target: reduce admin delays by 50% (measured by ticket SLAs).
- 60 day: collect post-offer NPS and hiring manager satisfaction; iterate playbook; document time saved per offer.
- 90 day: propose permanent resourcing (0.5FTE) if backlog reduced and managers report >=+0.3 satisfaction delta.

Calibration cues I want from manager (explicit asks during meeting):
- How does my current scope align with org priorities for H1? (direct question, expect a concrete list of priorities).
- Is the impact I’m showing consistent with expectations for a senior IC vs. a people-lead? (want calibration on level).
- What would you view as a decisive signal that I should shift focus toward a people-lead path?

Negotiation framing if they push back on resourcing:
- Offer a time-boxed pilot with clear success metrics and an automatic sunset if targets not met.
- Trade: I will deprioritize one non-critical cross-org project for the duration of the pilot.

Unresolved questions / things to surface live:
- Does leadership want a consolidated hiring-rubric owner, or should this remain distributed?
- If hiring freeze persists, what levers exist for temporary headcount for ops-critical blockers?
- Budget window for mid-quarter resource moves (who signs off; timeline?)

Notes to self (tone & logistics):
- Open the meeting with 90s recap (one sentence metric, one sentence story).
- Bring the single-sheet ROI (one pager) and the 30/60/90 plan in agenda.
- Keep ask categorical: "trial 3-month 0.5FTE for offer admin — we will measure X, Y, Z".
- Avoid getting bogged in design details; surface blockers and proposed mitigations.

Post-meeting followups to prep now:
- Draft contractor job description for 0.2 FTE triage role.
- Pull export of onboarding-metrics for the last 6 months and highlight trends.
- Prepare a one-slide ROI that shows time saved per offer and projected FTE-equivalent impact.

Micro-reflection prompts (for after the 1:1):
- What did I under-explain? What did they seem to care about most?
- Which counter-arguments came up? Were my mitigations persuasive?
- What next single action did we agree on? Put it in calendar within 48 hours.

Random brainstorming (scratch):
- Could we automate parts of the offer template with a tiny serverless script to pre-fill based on role metadata? Quick POC could save 10–15 minutes per offer.
- Pair with Recruiting analytics to build a dashboard that flags offers with >48h admin delay and auto-assigns triage.

End note: keep this doc concise; move final artifacts (one-pager, CSV exports) into a shared folder and link in Confluence page once pilot approved.

---
Version history (manual):
- 2025-11-12: initial scratch notes and framing.
- 2025-12-04: added pilot metrics and first evidence exports.
- 2026-01-20: refined 30/60/90 and behavioral stories after manager peer review.
- 2026-02-05: current; ready to copy into meeting agenda.
